I've farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life, same as my father. Around here, everyone grows winter wheat and summer maize — it's what the land is suited for, it's what the buyers want, and it's what I know. I have about 10 mu. I won't take risks with unfamiliar crops when I have a family to feed and loans to service.

For wheat, I'll sow in October after rotary tilling. I use improved varieties — the ag station has been pushing 济麦22 for years and it's reliable. I'll irrigate four times: before winter sets in, at jointing, at heading, and during grain fill. Water is expensive here with the pump, but skipping an irrigation on wheat is not something I'm willing to do. I apply urea in two splits — base and topdress at jointing — plus diammonium phosphate at sowing. Potassium I use less of; my soil already has decent K levels from years of straw return.

After wheat harvest in June, I go straight to maize without tilling — saves diesel and keeps moisture. I use a hybrid like 郑单958, which everyone around here has used for twenty years. Maize needs less hand-holding than wheat. Two irrigations — one at emergence if it's dry, one at tasseling. I top-dress urea once around the V6 stage.

Pesticides: wheat gets two sprays for aphids and rust, maize gets one or two depending on fall armyworm pressure, which has been getting worse lately.
